(B) The dopant is a pentavalent atom
(C) $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{h}} \neq \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}^2$

(E) In $n$ type semiconductor primary source of holes generation are thermal excitation.

questions.q: Take the breakdown voltage of the zener diode used in the given circuit as 6V. For the input voltage shown in the figure below, the time variation of the output voltage is: (Graphs drawn are schematic and not to the scale)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A diode in forward biased acts as short circuit, since current can smoothly pass in such case. The potential difference across this is negligible.

In reverse biased, initially, a negligible current can pass through it. When a voltage greater than the breakdown voltageV∘ applied across this, the potential difference remains at the breakdown voltage.

In this question, two diodes are connected in opposite polarity. At a time, one diode is in forward biased and other is reversed biased. For solution, we can ignore the forward-biased diode as its voltage is negligible. If the applied potential difference(input) across the reversed biased diode becomes greater than the breakdown voltageV∘, the potential difference across it will not increase and maintains at breakdown voltage.

In this question, the potential difference is changing direction and there will be one diode in reverse biased always. Hence, every peak will have a cut section and the range of the output graph will be -V∘, +V∘.

questions.q: The photodiode is used to detect the optical signals. These diodes are preferably operated in reverse biased mode because
options: fractional change in majority carriers produce higher forward bias current
fractional change in majority carriers produce higher reverse bias current
fractional change in minority carriers produce higher forward bias current
fractional change in minority carriers produce higher reverse bias current
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In photo–diode, the diode is connected in reverse bias, so initially the current will be very small. If the light is incident on the diode, its photons produce more minority charge carriers, which are called photo-generated charge carriers, due to which the reverse current increases.

In reverse bias, the width of the depletion region is more and the current is already very small, So the fractional charge in the current due to the light will be large.

questions.q:
Match the List I with List II

  List I   List II
A Intrinsic Semiconductor I Fermi-level near valence band
B n-type semiconductor II Fermi-level at middle of valence and conduction band
C p-type semiconductor III Fermi-level near conduction band
D Metals IV Fermi-level inside conduction band

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) The Fermi-level in an intrinsic semiconductor is nearly midway between the conductive and valence band.So, A→II.

(B) In the case of n-type semiconductor, the Fermi level is present just below the conduction band. So, B→III.

(C) Fermi level in a p-type semiconductor lies close to the top of the valence band. So, C→I

(D) In metals and semimetals the Fermi level lies inside at least one band i.e., inside conduction band. So, D→IV.

questions.q: For extrinsic semiconductors; when doping level is increased;
options: Fermi-level of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>- type semiconductors will not be affected.

Fermi-level of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math>-type semiconductor will go upward and Fermi-level of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>-type semiconductors will go downward.

Fermi-level of both p-type and n-type semiconductors will go upward for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>></mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> and downward for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo><</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>F</mi></msub><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>F</mi></msub></math> is Fermi temperature.

Fermi-level of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math>- type semiconductors will go downward and Fermi-level of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>- type semiconductor will go upward.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In n-type semiconductor pentavalent impurity is added. Each pentavalent impurity donates a free electron. So the Fermi-level of n -type semiconductor will go upward.
& In p-type semiconductor trivalent impurity is added. Each trivalent impurity creates a hole in the valence band. So the Fermi-level of p-type semiconductor will go downward.
